FINDING_ID: CC2_R4_CONV_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.82  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63  
DESCRIPTION: `_novel_classes()` implements novelty at the class level with an existentially-negative rule: a current equivalence class is marked novel only if none of its members are similar to any previous finding. This is inconsistent with `_compute_equivalence_classes()` using single-linkage clustering. A mixed class containing both one previously-seen finding and one genuinely new finding is treated as entirely non-novel, so the new finding contributes nothing to `kappa_set()` and cannot trigger `_veto()`. Concretely: if round r has findings A and B, with A similar to prior cumulative findings and B similar to A but not to any prior finding, single-linkage places {A,B} in one class; `_novel_classes()` then drops the whole class because A matches history. This creates false convergence and can suppress high-severity new findings.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Compute novelty against prior cumulative findings before or independent of current-round clustering. Two safe options: (1) classify novelty per member, then split current round into “novel support” vs “previously-covered support” before aggregating severity; or (2) when evaluating a current class, mark it novel if any member lacks a prior match, and define novel severity from the unmatched subset rather than the whole class. Do not let single-linkage transitivity erase partially novel content.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: CC2_R4_CONV_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58  
DESCRIPTION: `kappa_rate()` uses `len(get_round_classes(r)) / duration` as the failure-discovery rate proxy, i.e. total classes found in round r, not novel classes discovered in round r. Because repeated rediscovery of already-known findings still counts fully, the rate metric can remain low-convergence even when no new information is being produced. This contradicts the surrounding convergence design, where convergence is about exhaustion of new findings, and it also misaligns with `kappa_set()`, which is explicitly novelty-based. Example: if every later round repeats the same 5 classes with zero novelty, `kappa_set ≈ 1` but `kappa_rate` remains near baseline, blocking convergence indefinitely.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Base the rate metric on novel equivalence classes or novel aggregated severity per unit time, e.g. `lambda_hat(r) = |novel_classes(r)| / delta_t_r` or a severity-weighted novel rate. Keep total-class rate only as a separate workload/throughput diagnostic, not as a convergence component.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: CC2_R4_CONV_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.69  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.61  
DESCRIPTION: `kappa_rate()` anchors the baseline to round 1 if present, else round 0: `rate_1 = _rate(1) if 1 in self._round_findings else _rate(0)`. This is inconsistent with the documented formula `lambda_hat(1)` and becomes materially wrong under the already-reported FSM round-index ambiguity where `0` may correspond to non-iterative BLIND/SYNTH activity rather than the first iterative round. If round 0 is a qualitatively different phase, using it as the baseline distorts all subsequent `kappa_rate` values, producing either premature or delayed convergence depending on round-0 density and duration.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Require an explicit mapping from external round labels to iterative round numbers, or reject `kappa_rate` computation until a true first iterative round exists. At minimum, do not silently fall back from round 1 to round 0; instead return “insufficient data”/0.0 with a logged warning unless the caller explicitly designates round 0 as iterative.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: CC2_R4_CONV_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.57  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72  
DESCRIPTION: [CROSS-COMPONENT, UNVERIFIED FROM THIS SCOPE] `ConvergenceDetector` accepts arbitrary `round_idx` inserts via `add_round_findings()` and `get_cumulative_classes()` then aggregates `for r in range(round_idx + 1)`, implicitly assuming dense, gap-free round indices starting at 0. If the orchestrator/FSM skips indices, reuses an index across non-equivalent phases, or records only iterative rounds while omitting BLIND/SYNTH, cumulative history and baseline selection become dependent on absent rounds defaulting to empty findings. That can inflate convergence by treating missing rounds as no-findings rounds, and it compounds the existing cross-component ambiguity around `current_round`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Enforce a validated round schema at insertion time: monotone contiguous iterative indices only, or maintain an explicit ordered list of recorded iterative rounds and aggregate over that sequence instead of `range(round_idx + 1)`. Also separate phase identifiers from iterative round numbers.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: CC2_R4_CONV_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.55  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.49  
DESCRIPTION: `_compute_equivalence_classes()` assigns `flaw_class = members[0].flaw_class` to a cluster even though `_finding_similarity()` explicitly permits cross-`flaw_class` merging when textual similarity exceeds `tau_sim`. That means one equivalence class can contain heterogeneous flaw classes but expose only the first member’s class as the class label. This corrupts the semantic meaning of `FindingEquivalenceClass.flaw_class`, and any downstream consumer treating equivalence classes as class-homogeneous will make wrong inferences about support distribution or defect-type stability.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either forbid cross-class merging by requiring flaw-class compatibility in clustering, or represent clustered classes with `flaw_classes: Set[int]` / a distinguished “mixed” marker. Do not publish a single inherited flaw class when the class may be heterogeneous.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: CC2_R4_CONV_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.48  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.41  
DESCRIPTION: `add_round_findings()` accepts any `duration` value, and `kappa_rate()` converts non-positive durations into extremely large rates through `max(dt, 1e-10)`. A zero or negative duration therefore drives `kappa_rate` sharply negative, effectively preventing convergence for that round and potentially several decisions downstream, but without validation or explicit error. Since duration is an external measurement input, this silently turns bad telemetry into a semantic convergence veto.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate `duration > 0` in `add_round_findings()` and reject or warn on invalid values. If bad telemetry must be tolerated, mark the rate metric unavailable for that round rather than substituting `1e-10`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

Definitive stance: the main missed defects in this area are the partial-novelty loss caused by single-linkage plus class-level novelty, the non-novel rate metric being used as a convergence signal, and the unsafe fallback from iterative round 1 to round 0. These are substantive logic flaws in Convergence Detection itself; the round-index coupling issue remains cross-component and unverified from this scope.
